title: Define Dedicated Burst Capacity option requirements, success metrics, and beta customer criteria
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Objective
- Define clear product requirements for the Dedicated “Burst Capacity” option, including: customer-facing controls, guardrails, success metrics, and beta customer selection criteria.
- Ensure alignment across Product, Fleet, Routing, Control Plane, Telemetry, and SRE on what “good” looks like for pilot → GA.

Context
Dedicated customers are asking for short-lived capacity spikes without permanent over-provisioning. We are introducing a contractable burst mechanism that temporarily draws from controlled shared burst pools while preserving strict noisy-neighbor protections.

In scope (this ticket)
1) Requirements definition
- Customer problem statements + personas for burst:
  - predictable weekly/monthly spikes (batch jobs, marketing events)
  - sudden spikes (outage failover, news/virality) where best-effort burst is acceptable
- Explicit behaviors to specify in PRD (must be unambiguous for Eng + Docs):
  - When baseline is used vs burst is attempted
  - What happens when burst is denied (deny vs fallback; customer-visible semantics)
  - Required customer-visible guardrails configuration (initial v1):
    - max burst concurrency
    - max burst TPS (tokens/sec) and/or max requests/sec (by API route)
    - per-region enablement (or allowed regions list)
    - cooldown parameters (customer-configurable vs fixed defaults; if fixed, document)
    - optional time windowing (if not in v1, explicitly non-goal)
  - Tenant eligibility rules (beta): dedicated tier only; disallow for accounts with unresolved noisy-neighbor risk; ensure data residency constraints are not violated by burst routing.

2) Success metrics + dashboards/alerts requirements
Define metrics in two categories: customer outcomes and platform safety.

Customer outcome metrics (pilot)
- Burst admission success rate (per tenant, per region): % of burst attempts admitted when requested.
- Burst effective throughput uplift: delta TPS observed during spike periods vs baseline-only.
- Tail latency impact: p99 latency during burst periods relative to baseline SLO (should not regress beyond defined tolerance).
- Customer-reported “incident avoidance”: number of times burst prevented throttling/failed traffic.

Platform safety metrics (pilot)
- Neighbor protection: p99 drift on non-burst dedicated tenants sharing underlying infra should remain within agreed threshold.
- Pool saturation time: time at >X% utilization; reject rate correlation.
- Circuit breaker activations: count, duration, and reasons.
- Deny reason distribution (policy / saturation / cooldown / limits) to validate control-plane and routing semantics.
- Metric cardinality check: ensure we can attribute by tenant/pool/region without blowing up observability costs.

Pilot success criteria (exit)
- ≥ 99% policy correctness (no “bypassed admission” class bugs) and deterministic behavior across retries.
- No Sev1/Sev2 incidents attributable to burst that impact hosted fleet or baseline Dedicated commitments.
- Documented and rehearsed operational disablement/rollback procedures; SRE sign-off.

GA criteria (proposal; confirm with SRE + Infra)
- Stable SLO and alerting (burst admission SLO and neighbor p99 drift) with at least 2 cycles of clean oncall.
- Billing attribution available (even if initial invoicing stays shadow) with reconciliation report accuracy within acceptable delta.
- Docs + Console config UX shipped.

3) Beta customer selection criteria + list
Goal: 2–3 design partners that (a) have real spikes, (b) can provide fast feedback, (c) won’t create unacceptable operational risk.

Selection criteria
- Dedicated tenant already in good standing: stable baseline usage, no ongoing capacity disputes, and strong comms channel.
- Clear spike profile:
  - spike multiplier known (e.g., 3–10x baseline)
  - spike duration bounded (e.g., 10–90 minutes)
  - willingness to run controlled load tests with us
- Monitoring maturity: can share traces/metrics and tolerate brief deny/fallback behaviors during tuning.
- Compliance constraints: must allow bursting within agreed regions; no cross-region data residency ambiguity.
- Contracting readiness: accept beta terms (best-effort burst, shadow billing, clear guardrails).

Proposed beta candidates (to confirm with Sales/CS)
- Design partner: HubSpot company-10482 (needs burst for predictable spikes; technical sponsor engaged).
- Prospect: HubSpot company-10711 (burst is a key requirement; pricing sensitivity; peak-hour behavior).
- Existing customer: HubSpot company-10903 (historical scaling incidents; planned enrollment).

Out of scope / non-goals (ensure PRD states explicitly)
- Spot-market arbitrage / cross-cloud bursting.
- Customer-managed burst pools.
- Preemption guarantees beyond best-effort; v1 favors strict admission control over eviction.

Open questions (need answers before “Pilot Ready”)
- API semantics: When baseline is saturated, do we attempt burst automatically or only when customer opts-in per route?
- Deny semantics: 429 vs 503 and retry-after guidance; ensure consistent with Routing + Docs.
- Config defaults: are cooldown parameters customer-configurable in v1, or fixed with documented defaults?
- Included headroom vs overage: packaging decision for pilot (shadow billing) and GA direction.

Deliverables
- Updated PRD with finalized requirements + success metrics + beta criteria.
- One-page internal “Pilot Readiness Checklist” (owner/DRI list, gates, monitoring).
- Finalized shortlist of beta customers + rationale + owners (CSM/SE/PM).

DRIs
- Product requirements / PRD: Lauren Bishop
- Program coordination: Talia Benson
- Infra capacity sign-off: Vanessa Ortiz / Neha Kapoor
- SRE go/no-go: Sean Gallagher
- Metering attribution: Nadia Rahman

Risks
- Noisy-neighbor perception: even if isolation is preserved, customers will attribute latency changes to burst; need crisp customer comms and dashboards.
- Ambiguous fallbacks: if routing silently falls back to different model/region, may violate customer expectations; must document and potentially require opt-in.
- Observability cost: high-cardinality labels can balloon metrics; need early review with Telemetry.

Acceptance criteria
- PRD updated with:
  - customer-facing controls and defaults
  - explicit deny/fallback semantics
  - pilot/GA success metrics + thresholds
  - beta selection criteria + confirmed candidate list
- Pricing/packaging notes updated with:
  - beta terms (shadow billing, limits)
  - proposed GA packaging direction + open questions
- Alignment recorded from SRE + Infra (comment sign-off on this ticket).
